subject: Notify desktop users of unread notifications through end-to-end encrypted browser push

description.raw:
**As** a person who uses OpenProject as an installed desktop application  
**I want** to be told when new notifications arrive, even while the OpenProject window is closed  
**so that** I don't have to keep the application open to notice that something needs my attention.

**Acceptance criteria**

*   **Opt-in, per user and per device**
    
    *   A user can enable browser push from their notification settings. The browser's permission prompt appears only after that click, never on page load.
        
    *   Push is off by default. Enabling it on one device does not enable it on another; the settings page lists the user's subscribed devices and lets them revoke each one.
        
    *   Pausing reminders also pauses push.
        
*   **Administrators stay in control**
    
    *   An administrator can turn browser push off for the whole instance. Doing so deletes every stored subscription.
        
    *   Signing out, locking or deleting a user deletes that user's subscriptions.
        
*   **Nothing readable leaves the instance**
    
    *   A push carries no payload at all, so there is nothing for the browser vendor's push service (Google, Apple, Microsoft, Mozilla) to read or relay beyond an empty wake-up. Because there is no payload, no RFC 8291 encryption is needed and the browser's encryption keys are never stored.
        
    *   The service worker wakes, fetches the unread count and the latest unread event from the instance itself over the user's session, and builds the notification from that. Content level follows COMMS-48.
        
    *   Metadata is minimised: low urgency, a short time to live, one collapsing topic per user, and at most one push per user within a debounce window.
        
*   **What the user sees**
    
    *   One notification that replaces itself rather than stacking. With a single new event it names the actor and reason and the work package ("Alice mentioned you", "WP-123: Fix login") and clicking it opens that work package; with several it reads "N unread notifications" and opens the notification centre. A push that arrives after everything was read shows a silent "No unread notifications" and clears the badge, since browsers require a visible notification per push.
        
    *   The application icon's badge shows the same count when the push arrives.
        
    *   If the session has expired or the instance cannot be reached, the notification falls back to a generic "New activity in OpenProject" with no count.
        
*   **Supported browsers (desktop)**
    
    *   Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on macOS, including Safari web apps added to the Dock. Push is delivered while the browser is running, and on macOS Safari also while it is not.
        
*   **Documented**
    
    *   An administrator page states exactly what is sent and to whom, lists the push hosts the instance must reach, offers a reachability check per host, and explains that air-gapped instances cannot use browser push.
        

**Permissions and visibility considerations**

*   _To whom is this feature visible?_
    
    *   Every signed-in user, in every edition, on a supported desktop browser over HTTPS, once the administrator has left browser push enabled.
        
    *   The instance-wide switch sits with administrators under the existing email and notification settings.
        
*   _When is it not visible?_
    
    *   When the administrator has turned browser push off, or the instance cannot reach the push hosts.
        
    *   Over plain HTTP, in browsers without push support, and while the user has not opted in on that device.
        
    *   On phones and tablets, which are served by the OpenProject Mobile app.
